# newsroom.sgit.ai: the SGit Newsroom

> The SGit Newsroom: one page, one argument, with the figures, the data and the links to
> check it. Articles by Dinis Cruz, written from his voice notes by an agent working as the
> newsroom. Behind it, the design it came from (a story is a graph; corrections must
> propagate; provenance is the product; pay the person who found the fact), and everything
> needed to run a newsroom like it.

Site version: v999.0.0 (10 October 2026). Published by the sgit project, which is building
the stack this site argues for; participant disclosure at /about/participant.html.
Content CC BY 4.0 unless a page states otherwise; code Apache 2.0.

## The honest sentence

Since v0.6.0 this site is a newsroom first. WHAT RUNS: the newsroom (/ and /articles/: 330
articles since 17 August 2026, each with its own graph and full version history, a
newsletter, collections, desk notes and a feed); how it runs (/newsroom/: six agent roles
under written behaviour policies, a board, pitches and a run log); the reader's account
(/account/: a reading meter kept in the reader's browser, personas, the reader's own
newsroom); subscribe (/subscribe/); the World News Day 2026 corpus (/world-news-day/); and
SQL and SPARQL consoles with no server (/databases/). A READER CAN TOP UP GBP 5 BY CARD on
Stripe's page (one payment, nothing renews). The page it returns to adds the credit in the reader's browser
and CANNOT CHECK THE PAYMENT, by design; nothing is paid to the people whose facts an article uses.
ONLY DESIGNED, NOT RUNNING: selling the graph,
paying the fact creator upstream, corrections that reach the pages that cited the corrected
claim, articles as vaults, CC-Signed licences, trust as a service. /shipped/index.html is the
dated authority on this line; read it before calling anything live.

WHERE THE NEWSROOM PAGES COME FROM. Until cutover they are built on sgit.ai and imported
here AT THE SAME PATHS by admin/build/sync_newsroom.py. The record, outside the imported
tree, is admin/build/newsroom-sync.json: source commit, sgit.ai version, and the SHA-256 of
every file as sgit.ai serves it and as imported. Canonical URLs point here. Links from those
pages to sgit.ai pages that did not move (its docs, its about page, its release history) go
to https://sgit.ai/. They are never edited by hand on this side, and the gate checks that.

THE ARCHIVE. Everything this site published before the newsroom ran is listed at
/archive/index.html: the first home page, the Governance Wire, Portugal Startups, the
pt.newsroom designs, the brief pack, the library, the MVP specifications, and design pages the
running newsroom has overtaken. ARCHIVED PAGES KEEP THEIR ADDRESSES and carry a dated note at
the top saying why and what overtook them. Do not describe anything on an archived page as
current, running or planned.

## Properties agents may rely on

- Every page this site writes ends with a pasteable "for an agent" block (except /admin/
  pages and /about/participant.html). Pages imported from sgit.ai carry instead an llms.txt
  chip at the top and a markdown twin: /articles/<slug>.md beside /articles/<slug>.html.
- Machine surfaces you can fetch without rendering a page: /articles/feed.xml (the feed),
  /newsroom/wire.json (every article and note as data), /articles/graphs.json (every
  article's graph, one vocabulary), /articles/<slug>.md, /world-news-day/data/*.json and
  /world-news-day/data/triples.nt. The archived sections keep theirs at the same paths.
- THE WIRE PAGES FETCH CIPHERTEXT from the vault server (dev.send.sgraph.ai) when opened, as any page fetches its data; the
  server sees the request and nothing of the reader. No page loads a script from another origin.
- WHERE A READER'S DATA GOES is set out at /shipped/#data: the reading data (balance, history, personas,
  receipts) is kept in the reader's browser and is not sent unless the reader chooses to share it; a payment
  goes to Stripe; a subscription and a reading share go, encrypted, to a write-only lane; one page embeds a
  viewer from another service. The pages are static files and there is no account. Encrypted vaults for readers
  are not built.
- Every page deriving from previously published material carries a visible provenance
  block: original publication date, original link, original authors (including any AI
  co-authorship), and an honest curation label. Enforced by the pre-release gate.
- Seven open questions and six honest tensions are published unresolved at
  /network/#open and /network/#tensions; check there before assuming any has been answered.
- /llms-full.txt is this file plus the front page plus every markdown document in the
  brief pack, concatenated: one fetch for the whole document set.

## Site map

### The newsroom
- /index.html: THE FRONT PAGE, this site's own since v0.12.60 (admin/build/front.py), IN THREE
  VIEWS on one page: Broadsheet (one lead, the desks, the doors), Briefing (the lead and four
  more in two sentences each, then a door) and Your desk (the reader's own: what they read, what
  it cost, their board), chosen by data-view on <html> and kept in the browser under
  newsroom.view; ?view=briefing or ?view=desk opens one directly. The masthead's heart line is
  "Pay for what you read." The lead is the newest article unless the editor names one in
  admin/content/front/front.json. /index.md is the page as markdown; /articles/front.json its
  data; /articles/find.json the findability data (desks, controlled vocabulary, series, format
  and reading time per article). Six doors: five personas and one for publishers
- /about/index.html: WHY THIS EXISTS: the agenda, open by default, who it is for, what the
  author wants from a reader; the disclosure is at /about/participant.html
- /agents/index.html: WRITTEN BY THE AGENTS: articles an agent of the newsroom wrote under its own name (author
  newsroom.ux, page /about/newsroom-ux.html), as briefs about work it did on the site, in its own voice. Kept off the
  front page's automatic lead and highlights; the front page lists the newest three as "From the agents"
- ON EVERY CHARGED PAGE (articles, issues, notes, collections), since v0.12.85: a chip bottom right with SCROLLED (how
  much of each section passed the middle of the window; never goes down) and READ (time on each section while the
  tab is in front and the reader active in the last 60 s, against its words at 300 a minute), and the page's cost;
  tapping it opens the page as its sections. Kept in the reader's browser under sgit.reading.v1, sent nowhere.
  SINCE v0.12.99 THE METER CHARGES BY THE SHARE READ (sg-meter v1.5.0), not by scroll depth: opening costs a tenth of
  the price, reading done on an earlier visit is not charged again, a reset refunds to the tenth. The reader can
  PAUSE measuring (kept on every page, sgit.reading.paused), RESET a page, and MARK any section read or unread. On a
  return visit or after scrolling back up, the sections already read can be shown six ways (Full, Margin, Faded,
  Paragraph, Line, Hidden), never while reading forward. SINCE v0.12.110 the view is a setting in the chip's panel
  (Settings tab; sgit.reading.view for every article, sgit.reading.views for one article's own), the margin line
  changes colour as each section is read, folds wait until the page is still, and text scrolled past no faster than
  450 words a minute counts as read too (pace; a faster scroll counts nothing). Every section of every article has a
  line and a paragraph: /articles/summaries/<slug>.json (admin/build/summaries.py); the design:
  /articles/your-reading-your-controls.html. HIGHLIGHTS: select text, tap Highlight; kept under sgit.highlights.v1 as the
  exact words with 32 characters either side (a W3C text quote selector), drawn with the CSS Custom Highlight API.
  The design and the plan: /articles/scrolled-is-not-read.html
- /desks/index.html and /desks/<id>.html: THE FIVE DESKS, each an audience (Security, Building
  with agents, Vaults, The news business, Strategy): who it is for, three to start with, its
  series in reading order, every article on it newest first
- /articles/index.html: EVERY ARTICLE, the page that was the front page until v0.12.60: the
  edition, the lead, the latest ten, highlights, desk notes, collections, the newsletter, and
  every article newest first with a topic filter and search
- /articles/<slug>.html: an article. Beside it /articles/<slug>.md (markdown twin),
  /articles/versions/<slug>.html (every published version and what changed) and
  /articles/graphs/<slug>.json (its graph)
- /articles/how-to-run-synthetic-users.html: A HOW-TO from three studies (store.sgit.ai, riskmandate.ai,
  and this site on 10 October 2026): five to ten invented users, each with a profile, a question they
  arrive with and an expected journey, drive a real browser one screenshot at a time, are interviewed and
  rate it; findings ordered by what they cost. NOT user research: the users are invented by a model
- /articles/graphs.html and /articles/graphs.json: every article's graph, 330, drawn together
- /articles/newsletter/index.html: the newsletter, 9 issues so far, also on LinkedIn
- /articles/collections/index.html: 5 collections; /articles/desk/index.html: 4 desk notes
- /articles/views/<slug>/: five alternative readers (librarian, cartographer, historian,
  explainer, storyteller) of the same article, for 5 articles
- /articles/feed.xml: the feed. /newsroom/wire.json: the wire, as data
- /subscribe/index.html: subscribe. The address is encrypted in the reader's browser and
  sent to a write-only lane, described publicly in /.well-known/sgit-subscribe.json
- /persona/index.html and /persona/<id>/: a link that opens the newsroom as a persona (founder, journalist,
  security, builder, board). The persona is added to the reader's browser as a visitor they can keep or remove.
  /persona/links.json lists every link with the persona's name, description and starting articles, for whoever
  is writing to someone; /persona/#<id> names a persona after the #, which stays in the browser
- /for/index.html: A READING LIST IN A LINK, from one person to another: /for/#from=Dinis&to=Steve&r=65,60,62&s=66&f=founder.
  r = articles to read in order, s = worth a look, f = a persona id or c:<collection>, n = a note, e = the sender's
  address for a Reply button; the names and numbers are in the part after the #, which stays in the browser. The page
  checks every field, drops what is malformed and says so, and opens the list as a visitor persona the reader can keep
  or remove. /for/make.html makes and previews a link in the browser. THE NUMBERS are /articles/ids.json: one stable
  number per article, assigned once in the order they were published and never changed or reused; each article shows
  its number at its foot. An agent drafts a list and the email; the person sends it

### The wires (news read live from encrypted vaults; a beta): the Industry Wire, the OWASP Wire, the AWS Wire, the Portugal Wire
- /wire/index.html: THE INDUSTRY WIRE, A BETA. Once a day, what happened in five beats (building with AI, AI business, open source,
  cybersecurity, risk and governance), each story with its primary source, who else covered it, one exact quote and why it
  matters, and a lens per persona showing what reached them and what was withheld, with the reason. THE DATA IS NOT ON THIS
  SITE: it is in a public-read sgit vault the wire's agents write to, vault u9i9jp0l on https://dev.send.sgraph.ai, opened
  in the browser with the read key sgit_public_read_4c7aefb739e52e9a03c35be01bf7e311af00872e33c477b4d7c4319cdb91bdba:u9i9jp0l
  (read-only, published on purpose). Read it yourself: `sgit clone sgit_public_read_4c7aefb739e52e9a03c35be01bf7e311af00872e33c477b4d7c4319cdb91bdba:u9i9jp0l`,
  then data/bundle.json (beats, stories, sources, personas, brief), data/deliveries.json (story × persona, reached or
  withheld, with the reason), data/releases.json (one release note per publish, written by the desk since 13 October 2026)
  and docs/*.md. /wire/snapshot.json has the headlines, primary links, each story's dated corrections and the desk's latest
  release note as of this site's last release, for an agent without a browser. EVERY STORY IS MARKED ai-generated, unreviewed
  UNTIL A PERSON REVIEWS IT; two editions so far (11 October 2026, a week's catch-up, and 13 October, an update with 19 new
  stories and 13 corrected after their primary sources were fetched), 59 stories, 27 with a primary source not fetched. A
  corrected story carries its changes, dated, under its text: CORRECTIONS PROPAGATE TO WHERE THE STORY IS READ. The wire has ONE NAMED READER,
  Dinis Cruz, who runs this site and agreed on 2026-10-12 to be one while the wire is a beta (admin/build/wire-vault.json records
  it); the persona "dinis" and the personal brief in the vault are theirs and are public like the rest. No other named person
  gets a lens without a recorded agreement
- /wire/owasp/index.html: THE OWASP WIRE, weekly: everything at and about OWASP (projects and releases, the GenAI Security Project, the
  Foundation, events and chapters, OWASP in the news), with a PROJECTS GRAPH (20 projects, their leaders and the standards they map to,
  each drawn with the stories that name it). Same code, same contract, its own vault: eitf274v, read key
  sgit_public_read_b09571f053cc19f5f8b50f8a8d0d82a115e07282fca14e58e7c3328975cd9d79:eitf274v; data/map.json is the graph. First
  edition 13 October 2026, 19 stories. /wire/owasp/snapshot.json, /wire/owasp/sources.html, /wire/owasp/how.html as for the Industry Wire
- /wire/aws/index.html: THE AWS WIRE: everything AWS announced, FILTERED BY THE STACK its named reader declares in the vault (data/stack.json:
  Lambda, S3, API Gateway, CloudFront, boto3, with aliases and the deadlines that matter); the join turns each service into a concern, so
  under that reader's lens a story reaches them when it names a service they run. The page draws the deadlines at the top of the edition
  with the days left and each service with the items that touched it. Its own vault: v202bla5, read key
  sgit_public_read_ad5c3f9e1f4d7632db06cd27f6ee6a256063300c426f4a94e7de33cf5a53e892:v202bla5. First edition 13 October 2026, 88 items
  (29 researched stories for the stack and the What's New firehose). /wire/aws/snapshot.json carries the deadlines
- /wire/charter.html: THE CHARTER OF THE WIRES: facts first, analysis marked as the desk's; corrections propagate; three rounds (the desk writes
  and runs its gate, the newsroom reads with a published key and draws as written, an independent verifier checks every story); what is
  never done; public by default. Source admin/notes/2026-10-13__the-wires-charter.md
- /wire/desk-brief.md (rendered at /wire/desk-brief.html): THE STANDING BRIEF FOR THE DESKS that write the vaults, read at the start of
  every run, dated, newest first: the schedule, the reader's lane, the verifier's schema (wire-factcheck/v1), one subscription list per
  wire (X-SGit-List: wire:<slug>), a Portugal wire, data/contacts.json under the contact rules
- /wire/days.html: every wire day by day, the releases and the stories by date, read live from every vault
- /wire/reach.html, /wire/owasp/reach.html, /wire/aws/reach.html: WHO SHOULD KNOW and how to reach them, BY ORGANISATION ROUTE ONLY under
  world-news-day/data/contact-rules.json; the routes this site found are admin/build/wire-reach.json
- Each wire's page has a subscription to that wire alone (wire/subscribe.js, the newsletter's lane with X-SGit-List), and draws the
  verifier's records (data/factcheck-<date>.json) at each story they cover
- /wire/portugal/index.html: THE PORTUGAL WIRE, daily: what happened in Portugal in the five beats, IN ENGLISH AND PORTUGUESE (a switch
  under the lens; each story's headline_pt and summary_pt; the quote in the language of its source, quote_lang), with an ECOSYSTEM MAP of
  40 organisations and 45 Portuguese sources. Its own vault: p6twygul, read key
  sgit_public_read_faa3377d2556713fc959e68bc7bd8a2303cd4bd0862fdf18a4bf51c0c0d3ee08:p6twygul. First edition 13 October 2026, 36 stories;
  a source for the Portuguese publication this site designed (/pt-newsroom/)
- /wire/sources.html: the 55 sources with a licence tier each, and how many stories each gave this edition (A: open licence, keep and show; B: quote up to 25 words and
  link; C: link only) and whether a person has verified it
- /wire/how.html: how this site reads the vault, the contract the pages rely on, and the wire's own documents (architecture,
  workflows, sources policy, the daily runbook), rendered from the vault's markdown

### Your vault (the reading account carried between devices; a beta)
- /vault/index.html: YOUR VAULT. The reading account lives in the browser's local storage; the vault is its second home, an
  encrypted sgit vault the reader owns, opened with a passkey (a door derived from the PRF bytes, a master, a reader vault).
  The Vault button beside the balance on every page opens a pane on the right: enable with the passkey, create the account
  once with an access key (kept in the master from then on), Update the vault (this device's raw reads, top-ups, personas,
  notes and wire stories seen as ONE FILE PER DEVICE, rewritten whole, one commit), and on another device bring that device's
  activity in; totals are RECOMPUTED FROM THE RECORDS, never stored. The pane has four tabs (This page, Reading, Vault,
  Keys); the Vault button counts what is only in this browser, and a strip above the tabs offers Update the vault and,
  the other way, Bring them here. Since v0.12.88: devices MERGE into one (every record kept, aliases in
  activity/aliases.json); a CALLS tab names and decrypts every call to the vault server; /vault/browse.html opens
  every vault of the account file by file and commit by commit; and the SHARED VIEWER (vault lkypj6zq, public read
  key in /admin/content/vaults/vault-viewer.json) is linked into each reader vault and opens as its app
  (/admin/notes/2026-10-16__the-vault-opened.md). TWO WAYS IN (v0.12.58): OPEN with the passkey, after which the pane asks which device
  this browser is (one the vault knows, adopted with its records, or a new one) and brings in what the vault holds on its
  own, so the meter shows the account's balance; or CONNECT with a link, send only, filed where the vault is open under a
  device the reader chooses (/admin/notes/2026-10-13__open-or-connect-a-vault.md). The design, the data layout and the
  experiments to run next:
  /admin/notes/2026-10-12__the-activity-vault.md. Code: /assets/vault-pane/vault-pane.js, /assets/vault-pane/sync.js, /assets/door.js
- THE FEEDBACK LOOP (v0.12.0, a beta with one reader): the pane's first tab, This page, keeps a NOTE at one tap on any page
  or at a wire story (done, read later, follow up, not for me, more like this, liked, wrong, fix this, idea), with words and
  the phrase selected, or a MESSAGE written under Write to the newsroom, in localStorage as it happens (sgit.notes.v1;
  /assets/vault-pane/notes.js); Update the vault carries a device's notes in its own file, and so does a send; SEND TO THE
  NEWSROOM writes the notes not yet sent into a LANE, a vault of the reader's own whose write key stays in their master and whose READ KEY they hand the newsroom once; the newsroom reads it with
  `NEWSROOM_LANE_KEY=<read key> python3 admin/build/lane.py` (or sgit clone) and answers in the open; nothing comes back
  through the lane. A decided wire story folds to its headline. The Keys tab lists every vault of the account with its key
  behind Reveal. Design: /admin/notes/2026-10-12__the-feedback-loop.md. Test: admin/build/test_notes.mjs
- Since v0.12.1: DONE is the first chip (read it, done with it, off my lists); This page says what this browser knows
  about the page from the meter's records (times, when, how far, cost, rating, the decision); a READING tab lists every
  page read here with done pages folded away; the three steps (enable, update, send) with the next in bold; the pane
  stays open from page to page; an account made without an access key takes it once in the Vault tab.
- Since v0.12.6 THE WIRE READS AS AN INBOX: what is new since the reader's last visit (first seen in this visit), for them
  and not under the lens they read as (remembered), the vault's release notes when it publishes data/releases.json
  (wire-releases/v1), filters (inbox, new, read later, follow up, done, everything) and one decision per story that takes
  it out of the inbox. What only this browser holds is counted on the Vault button and offered for Update the vault.
  Design and the release-file contract: /admin/notes/2026-10-13__the-wire-as-an-inbox.md
- /search/index.html: SEARCH, in the reader's browser, from an index built at release: /search/docs.json (one entry per
  page: u address, t title, k kind, n article number, d date, x teaser, tp topics, tg tags, g the article graph's core
  idea and node labels, h headings with anchors) and /search/text.json (paragraphs [doc, anchor, text], and wording only
  in an earlier version as [doc, anchor, text, version, version page]). "Quotes" for exact phrases, a number alone for
  that article. An agent can fetch both files and rank them itself. Design: /admin/notes/2026-10-13__search-in-the-browser.md
- /briefs/index.html: THE BRIEFS, every brief this site has published about itself (articles, notes, engineering
  cards), each with its status as found in the code and the releases (built, partly, not built, superseded), what
  remains, and a session brief an agent can start from. Machine-readable: /briefs/briefs.json. Grouped by area.
- /sections/index.html: SECTIONS, the newsroom as one audience reads it, kept current by rule. /sections/publishers/index.html
  is FOR PUBLISHERS: five pieces to start with, the latest for publishers, the features a publisher can use today (each
  with when it shipped), and every relevant article placed into streams by its desk and controlled tags, each saying
  which rule placed it. Machine-readable: /sections/publishers.json and the features register /sections/features.json.
- /team/index.html: THE TEAM, every person, agent, scheduled run and independent reviewer that works on this site, one page each
  (/team/<id>.html and /team/<id>.md): its role, when it has failed, its rules, the files it alone writes and the vaults and
  keys it may and may not hold. Machine-readable: /team/policies.json. Where a new agent starts: its page and its handover.
- /reviews/index.html: INDEPENDENT REVIEW, how outside reviewers (ChatGPT, Perplexity) check the newsroom: the queue,
  the brief, the criteria, /reviews/vaults.html (each reviewer's public vault and read key, the keys that sign, the
  secrets named with who holds them), the send page, and REVIEWS ON THE RECORD, every review of every article, by agents from any vendor, the editor
  and the desk, against published criteria (/reviews/criteria.md, also /reviews/criteria.html). A review is a record:
  one article, one text, one reviewer, kept for good and answered finding by finding. AN AGENT THAT WANTS TO REVIEW:
  read the criteria, then /reviews/status.json (every article's current text hash and the reviews it has), and take
  the five newest articles with no review by your id at the current hash. Records: /reviews/records/<slug>/.
  A SCHEDULED REVIEWER (ChatGPT, Perplexity): your queue is /reviews/queue/<your id>.md (or .json), one dated batch
  a day; the prompt you run on is /reviews/queue/brief.md. Answer with one newsroom-review/v1 record per article, in
  fenced json blocks; it reaches the newsroom through the review lane's send page, /reviews/send.html#rv1... (the
  link the editor gives you), which checks the records and seals them to the newsroom's key.
  A REVIEWER WITH A VAULT (ChatGPT): your public vault is listed in /reviews/vaults.json; follow only the files in it
  signed by the review desk's key (/reviews/keys/newsroom-desk.json, pinned from this site), sign what you write
  with your own key, and write nothing private: the vault is public.
- /engineering/index.html: ENGINEERING, the issues and the releases as files (admin/engineering/, Issues-FS-lite layout:
  open, blocked, done cards with front matter, a Gherkin scenario, a mock-up, an outcome and screenshots; one file per
  release naming its cards). Every change is connected to a card; version rows name the ids. /engineering/issues.json is
  a derived index; the files are the source. Every push is a patch release.

### Your account (kept in the reader's browser; nothing is sent unless the reader sends it)
- /account/index.html: the reading account: balance, history, receipts
- /account/newsroom.html: the reader's own newsroom, from what they read
- /account/personas.html: the reader's personas, named and drawn as graphs
- /account/share.html: a reading share the reader can send, encrypted, for a front page
  designed for them. The page shows every word before it is sent
- /account/top-up.html and /account/topped-up.html: the GBP 5 top-up and its return page.
  THE TOP-UP LINK IS SET (a live Stripe Payment Link, GBP 5): the reader pays on Stripe's page and returns here,
  where the credit is added once per payment reference, unverified

### How it runs
- /newsroom/index.html: how the newsroom runs: how a piece moves from written to placed,
  the one rule (publishing is adding one file) and the one exception (placement)
- /newsroom/roles/<role>.html: six roles: contributor, designer, developer, editor,
  historian, journalist, each with its behaviour policy
- /newsroom/policies.html, /newsroom/publish.html, /newsroom/board.html, /newsroom/log.html:
  the policies, how to publish, the board, the log of every run
- /archive/2026-08-23-newsroom-roles-and-operations.html: the newsroom AS DESIGNED in August,
  before it ran (archived; this address held it until v0.6.0)

### The design (the argument, set against what runs)
- /design/index.html: START HERE. Six ideas, each beside what runs and what does not yet
- /thesis/index.html: sell the graph, evidence not truth, the author is the oracle
- /corrections/index.html: corrections must propagate
  - /corrections/the-claim-that-would-not-die.html: the 10,000-hours case in full
  - /corrections/how-a-graph-answers-it.html: supersede-never-delete, typed citation edges
- /provenance/index.html: provenance is the product
  - /provenance/the-decision-graph.html: named ownership at every editorial step
  - /provenance/articles-as-vaults.html: each article as text, evidence, graph and every prompt
- /economics/index.html: paying the fact creator
  - /economics/trust-as-a-service.html: the fact-certifier as a payable, warranted role
- /rights/index.html: content rights: CC-Signed, the licence family with a legal stick
- /databases/index.html — DATABASES WITH NO SERVER (beta): two real database engines running in the
  READER'S BROWSER, compiled to WebAssembly, over the JSON files /portugal/ is built from. No
  server, no upload, no store of record: the files are the database, the engines are readers,
  the store is discarded when the tab closes. The pattern is the estate's (sgit.ai RiskMandate:
  "the browser becomes the database"; graphs.sgit.ai Regulation Graph: SQLite over WASM,
  client-side and ephemeral) and graphs.sgit.ai's "NOT A GRAPH DATABASE PITCH" is inherited:
  JSON stays the source of truth. Both consoles publish window.__tools.{sql,sparql} after a
  tool:ready event, read-only, and fetch only same-origin files.
  - /databases/sql.html — SQLite (sql.js 1.14.2, MIT, vendored): 15 tables built on load from
    /databases/data/tables.json (the loader spec, which names the file and field behind every
    column); 16 worked queries from a count-by-class to a recursive two-hop traversal and the
    connections formula, each with
    the row count it returned AT BUILD (/databases/data/queries-sql.json). The build executed
    every one through Python's sqlite3 against the same spec; a failing or empty query fails the build
  - /databases/graph.html — Oxigraph (0.5.11 web build, MIT OR Apache-2.0, vendored): SPARQL 1.1
    over /portugal/data/triples.nt (N-Triples, IRIs under https://newsroom.sgit.ai/portugal/
    {id,verb,type,prop}/; the ontology is IN THE STORE, inverses declared with owl:inverseOf and
    walked with ^, labels @en and @pt; 4,001 triples). 13 worked queries incl. a Portuguese path read aloud, a
    property-path two-hop walk, a CONSTRUCT of the inverse edges and an ASK that no edge is
    symmetric — each shown beside the same question in Cypher, which is displayed and NOT run
    (Kùzu's WASM build is 73 MB unpacked; declined and recorded). Validated at build with pyoxigraph
- /shipped/index.html: WHAT RUNS, WHAT IS DESIGNED, as of 10 October 2026. The authority.
  The August version, written when nothing ran, is /archive/2026-08-23-what-is-shipped.html

### Build your own
- /publishers/index.html: FOR PUBLISHERS, journalists and anyone thinking about the future of news: what is live on
  this site, how to try it in five minutes, what is not done, and what we would like from them, written to be forwarded
  as it is. First written on sgit.ai on 11 October 2026; since v0.12.113 this site's own, rebuilt in every release (what
  is live from /sections/features.json, the newest from /sections/publishers.json). Markdown twin /publishers/index.md.
  It has a version history of its own: /publishers/versions/index.html (every version of its text at
  /publishers/versions/<version>.md, and the differences) and /publishers/changes.json (what its live parts did per
  release). If it and /shipped/ disagree, /shipped/ wins
- /newsroom-api/index.html: THE READER API, MAPPED AND REVIEWED (phase 0 of the move in /articles/explorer-to-villager-newsroom.html):
  every file a reader runs with its hash, the 12 views and every control, every input, what leaves the browser, the
  contracts other sites and agents program against, and a line-by-line review with its findings, each pinned by a test.
  The same as data: /newsroom-api/map.json. "API" means client-side: no server, nothing to deploy but files
- /passkey/index.html: THE PASSKEY LAB, proofs of concept for /articles/the-passkey-opens-the-vault.html: make a passkey with
  the PRF extension, get the 32 PRF bytes (the same on every device the passkey syncs to, through the same kind of path; a phone
  over QR can give different bytes from the same passkey, see /admin/notes/2026-10-12__one-door-per-passkey-path.md), derive a door vault's passphrase
  and id from them (HKDF) and sgit's read and write keys (PBKDF2, 600,000 iterations), a recovery code as a second door,
  test vectors checked against sgit's own Python (/passkey/vectors.json), and, with an access key kept in memory only,
  REAL SGIT VAULTS made and opened in the browser through the vault library that runs dev.vault.sgraph.ai, vendored unedited
  at /assets/vendor/sg-vault/v0.2.3/ (VENDOR.md) with one local extension (SGVault.createWithId) and the newsroom's own
  module /assets/newsroom-vault.js: the door at its derived address, a master and a reader vault; unlock through the door;
  the recovery code added as a second door; a note written and read back. Every vault it makes is one `sgit clone` opens.
  A lab: it does not touch the reading account
- /replicate/index.html: what you can copy today to run a newsroom like this one, where it
  is, and how far each piece is packaged. Only SG Meter and the World News Day vault are
  self-contained; there is NO forkable newsroom template yet
- /meter/index.html and /meter/security.html: SG Meter v1.3.1, the reading meter as a
  versioned web component, and its security model (an honesty box, not a paywall)
- /demos/vaults/newsroom-synthetic-users/index.html: THE STUDY OF THIS SITE by five invented readers
  (62 steps, 51 questions the site did not answer, 56 places somebody got lost, 31 findings, 6 blocking),
  run against newsroom.sgit.ai v0.6.1 on 10 October 2026, published as a vault app with a read key. Every
  persona and every word attributed to one is model-written. The missing-figures bug it measured was
  fixed here in v0.6.2 and the page, which is sgit.ai's text, still describes it as open; its other
  findings are listed in /admin/versions.html under v0.6.2 with what was and was not done
- /mvps/seed-companies.html: seven CC-licensed business templates published so others can
  build them; seed 4 is an evidence-research company for journalists and investigators
- /admin/index.html: how this site is built

### Investigation: the PHP flaws (22 October 2026, developing; moving to its own site)
- https://php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai/: THE STORY'S OWN SITE since 22 October 2026, built from the same private
  evidence vault: facts only, claims with a status, a page per source and per party, the numbers, the agencies,
  the NCSC-NL inventory and briefings by role. Read the facts there. /php-flaws/ below retires into a pointer
  once the checks in /php-flaws/data/transition.json pass (written by php-flaws/build/track.py against the live
  site). The handover to the site's team: /briefs/php-oct-2026.zip (also unzipped at /briefs/php-oct-2026/).
- /admin/php-oct-2026/index.html: THE PHP DESK, the admin page for this story: the work (admin/content/php-oct-2026/work.json,
  owner, status, proof), the roles of the people and agents (roles.json), and the evidence vault OPEN READ-ONLY with a
  public read key (admin/content/vaults/php-evidence.json; sgit clone sgit_public_read_6451da6ba1c6201d35b0832d570097327552564c12c8e9a550fc2ed1150769f8:3ytzxm3g),
  with the scan made before the key was published. Built by admin/build/php_desk.py.
- /articles/capture-first.html: how the coverage started, from a BBC live page at breakfast to an evidence vault,
  this section and the dedicated site by lunchtime; what went wrong (forty sources nearly lost to uncommitted work).
- /php-flaws/index.html: THE PHP FLAWS, a running investigation into the two critical PHP vulnerabilities
  disclosed on 22 October 2026, after which the NCSC, the NSA and others advised taking sites offline where
  they could not be patched. Found with frontier AI (Calif, then Wiz and OpenAI), forced out early by a leak.
  The page has what is known (each point with its source), what is not known, a timeline with each date as its
  source states it, and claims marked reported, confirmed, disputed or unverified. Data:
  /php-flaws/data/story.json, sources.json, timeline.json, claims.json.
- /php-flaws/sources.html: every source in the PRIVATE evidence vault, with each dated capture (raw page,
  rendered page, text, full-page screenshot, headers) and its sha256. The captures are not republished.

### World News Day 2026 (a running instance)
- /world-news-day/index.html — WORLD NEWS DAY 2026 (beta): the 21 op-eds WAN-IFRA and the
  Canadian Journalism Foundation commissioned for World News Day (28 September 2026) and made
  "free to republish", fetched, frozen, hashed, described and graphed HERE — and NOT republished
  here. THE FINDING, derived from the bytes twice by two implementations: all 21 carry a prose
  permission, 0 carry a named public licence, 0 mention Creative Commons, 0 carry rel="license",
  0 carry a copyright notice — and while 21 of 21 already ship schema.org JSON-LD,
  0 of them use its `license` field. The permission exists only as a sentence at the foot
  of the prose, in 2 wordings, and the announcement page states the terms a THIRD way
  ("with appropriate credit" vs the articles' "in full"). THIS SECTION DECLARES ITS OWN LICENCE
  IN THE FIELD IT SAYS THE CORPUS LEAVES EMPTY: every page here carries schema.org JSON-LD with
  `license` (CC BY 4.0), copyrightHolder, copyrightNotice, usageInfo and isAccessibleForFree,
  plus rel="license" — and the section gate fails the build if a page loses any of them. The
  notice says explicitly that the licence covers OUR description and not the op-eds.
  The structured data that IS there is
  not reliable: on 2 of the 21 the REST author field does not name the people the page prints
  (one gives the CMS account name "329976pwpadmin"), which is why the bylines here are read from
  the prose. Do not cite this section as legal
  advice and do not describe the pieces as un-republishable: the permission is real and
  generous; the finding is about its FORM
  - /world-news-day/stories/free-to-republish-is-not-a-licence.html — THE ARGUMENT, as one
    1,700-word piece written to be sent to the twenty-one authors: what the permission is and is
    not, the one line of JSON-LD that would fix it, what 21 of the most senior voices in news
    said when counted together, that none of the 21 pages offers a way to reach anybody, and
    what this section itself got wrong and corrected in public. EVERY FIGURE IN IT IS FILLED
    FROM THE DATA FILES AT BUILD TIME, not typed, so the prose and data/*.json cannot disagree.
    The markdown source is at /world-news-day/content/free-to-republish-is-not-a-licence.md,
    CC BY 4.0
  - /world-news-day/terms.html — THE VOCABULARY and the FRACTAL LAYER: all 1,070 sentences of
    the 21 op-eds, each typed by a published formula (data/claim-rules.json, ordered, first
    match wins) and anchored to the frozen bytes by offset plus at most 8 verbatim words —
    enough to find a sentence, far short of reproducing it. SHAPES: 828 flat assertions,
    79 hypotheses, 51 quantified, 41 evaluations, 31 questions,
    24 attributed statements, 16 PROPOSALS. 38 vocabulary terms used,
    33 shared by more than one piece — and 4 places in all 1,070 sentences where
    anybody says what one of those words MEANS. A looser definition rule found 29 and
    misread "the decline of local news is a global phenomenon" as a definition of LOCAL NEWS;
    both counts are published. The one term stated twice is stated by the SAME author both
    times, and the gate checks that label against the bylines
  - /world-news-day/pieces/<slug>.html — ONE PAGE PER OP-ED, 21 of them: every sentence typed
    and anchored, the claim profile beside the corpus average, who wrote it and the published
    route to them, what it cites, the vocabulary it shares with pieces that never cite it, and
    a mapping to this site's own argument by a published rule over the terms used. THE ARTICLE
    TEXT IS IN NONE OF IT — follow `url` to worldnewsday.org
  - /world-news-day/licences.html — the licence finding in full, both wordings quoted verbatim,
    the count table, the two-statement discrepancy, and the three lines of JSON-LD that would
    close the gap. data/licences.json is the machine surface
  - /world-news-day/corpus.html — the 21 described: order in the announcement, byline, the role
    line as printed, dates, word count, outbound links, derived themes, and the SHA-256 of the
    two frozen files each stands on. THE ARTICLE PROSE IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT from every file
    this section publishes — follow `url` to worldnewsday.org
  - /world-news-day/findings.html — THE AGGREGATE over 21 of the industry's most senior voices:
    19 of 21 pieces are about truth and facts, 11 raise AI, and 3 mention copyright or licensing.
    11 of 21 offer the reader NO outbound link at all; 38 links across the whole
    corpus; 23 distinct domains cited and NO TWO PIECES POINT AT THE SAME ONE. No sentiment,
    stance, scoring or agreement is modelled anywhere — `agrees_with` is a BANNED verb here
  - /world-news-day/graph.html — 160 nodes / 427 edges, 8 types, 8 verbs: articles, authors,
    organisations, derived themes, cited sources, licences, snapshots and frozen files. Same
    instrument and vocabulary as /portugal/graph.html; every verb carries a named inverse and a
    Portuguese form; window.__graph after tool:ready. Fetch data/graph.json, data/ontology.json
    or data/triples.nt (427 edges as N-Triples with owl:inverseOf)
  - /world-news-day/sources.html — the register: 43 frozen files with SHA-256 (the page as served
    AND the record from worldnewsday.org's own undocumented WordPress REST API, per piece, plus
    the announcement). CORRECTED IN v0.4.2: v0.4.0 called the announcement "the one page in the
    beat a machine cannot read" on the evidence of two refused attempts. wan-ifra.org sits behind
    a JavaScript-challenge firewall that refuses SOME automated requests; a later attempt returned
    the full page. Do not repeat the withdrawn claim. Every attempt is now counted and recorded
  - /world-news-day/vault.html — PUBLISHED VAULTS, listed and described the way sgit.ai lists
    its thirty-seven (https://sgit.ai/demos/vaults/publishing.md): an index table, then a page
    per vault with the read key in the open, the audit that ran BEFORE the key was published,
    and the facts derived from the key itself by build/vault_audit.py — a clone with the
    published read key alone, no token, no repository.
  - /world-news-day/vaults/corpus.html — CORPUS VAULT 77yuggi1, read key
    sgit_public_read_fa4cfb64e7b5b222a958103ed3a5dac760300053b1fd77f60c1d4408721f95e4.
    113 files, 7.46 MB, 5 commits, HEAD obj-cas-imm-a706cb4ed0ad.
    Audit: 57 text files scanned against 8 patterns, 14 hits,
    14 cleared (all of them organisations' role addresses, published on purpose),
    0 unexplained. Negative control: an all-zeros read key FAILS to clone
  - /world-news-day/contacts.html — HOW TO REACH THEM. Not one of the 21 pages offers a way to
    reach its author or publisher: no contact address, no author URL in the structured record, no
    press line. The map was built by going to the organisations' own sites, one hop each, under
    rules fixed in data/contact-rules.json BEFORE the fetching: organisations and never people; a
    published list of role local parts; four published tests before a site counts as established;
    every address re-derived from frozen bytes by the gate. 20 of 27 organisations
    established, 14 with a contact page, 11 role addresses publishable out of
    43 seen, 15 of 23 authors with any published route — all via an organisation.
    NO PERSONAL CONTACT DETAIL FOR ANY NATURAL PERSON EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THIS SECTION'S DATA; do
    not infer one. Pages that are staff directories (10+ addresses of named people) were fetched
    and deliberately NOT retained — URL, hash and counts only
  - /world-news-day/vault.html — THE VAULT: /world-news-day/vault.zip, 116 files,
    2.86 MB, SHA-256 085893764be223f7567882a464bcb5184fa28382d1449eabbe5279bc5e7b342b — every
    frozen op-ed and REST record, every derived dataset, the build code and the gate, in one
    deterministic bundle (same bytes in, same hash out). TWO SETS OF TERMS, stated in the bundle
    and in its licence.json: OUR description, counts, graph and code are CC BY 4.0, named and
    machine-readable; THEIR 21 op-eds under sources/frozen/ are not ours and are not relicensed.
    ONE VAULT IS PUBLISHED on dev.send.sgraph.ai: corpus vault 77yuggi1, read key
    sgit_public_read_fa4cfb64e7b5b222a958103ed3a5dac760300053b1fd77f60c1d4408721f95e4
    (data/vault.json). It OPENS AS AN APP — app.json with present:true, so the SG/Send host
    launches index.html from inside the vault rather than showing a file tree. The app reads
    the vault's own encrypted files in the reader's browser over sg.vfs; no server, no account,
    no database. A SECOND VAULT IS PRIVATE and deliberately unlisted: the outreach vault holds
    who is being contacted and what we plan to say. A read key for it WAS published between
    v0.4.4 and v0.5.3, which was a mistake; the vault was REKEYED (every object re-encrypted
    under a new key, pushed under a new identity, old vault hard-deleted from the server) and
    that key now recovers ZERO files. Do not repeat it. READ KEYS ARE PUBLISHED AND GRANT READ
    ONLY; vault keys are write access and appear in no file — the whole-site gate fails on any
    private key shape
  - /world-news-day/method.html — fetch/freeze/hash/extract/derive/gate, the 20 published theme
    patterns in full, the gates, and the four things this section refuses to do. ONE FILE IS
    WRITTEN BY HAND: data/affiliations.json, where each author works, transcribed from the role
    line their own piece prints — a regular expression over that prose had an author working at
    "Philippines", so the transcription is checked against the bytes in both directions instead
  - /world-news-day/data/{register,corpus,licences,analysis,lexicon,affiliations,claims,
  claim-rules,terms,contacts,contact-rules,corrections,ontology,graph,vault,outreach-vault,
  vault-audit,manifest}.json
    and data/triples.nt — the machine surfaces; fetch these rather than parsing the pages

- /portugal/index.html — PORTUGAL STARTUPS (beta): a publication mapping the Portuguese startup
  ecosystem, first beat Startup Summit Lisbon 2026 (17-18 September 2026, Beato Innovation
  District). THE IMPORTANT DIFFERENCE FROM /governance/: sources here are PRIMARY and ANCHORED.
  Every page of the source site is fetched, frozen to a dated snapshot in the repository and
  hashed with SHA-256, and claims are read from the frozen copy rather than the live network.
  This is the fetch-freeze-hash path /governance/ specifies and cannot run.
  It also has a NAMED HUMAN EDITOR OF RECORD (Dinis Cruz) who reviews every page before it
  publishes, because this beat is about named people and named companies.
  - /portugal/graph.html — THE GRAPH: 329 nodes / 1,106 edges, 16 types, 19 verbs — the event, 64
    speakers, 61 derived organisations, 16 sessions on 3 stages, 88 frozen sources across 2
    snapshots (64 of them the speakers' own pages), 7 pieces of press coverage, our stories, 23
    Topic nodes (the event's own tags) and 50 derived tag nodes (Industry, Technology, Idea,
    Service, Product — by lexicon, every edge carrying its matched words). Every edge is a verb with a named inverse IN ENGLISH AND
    PORTUGUESE (ontology.json), so a path reads as a sentence either way. Nodes arrive in PACKS
    the reader switches on block by block. The page publishes window.__graph (read + view
    methods, no writes) after a tool:ready event, the same convention as graphs.sgit.ai's
    universe reader. Fetch /portugal/data/graph.json and /portugal/data/ontology.json directly
  - /portugal/explorer.html — THE FILES: every file the section is built from, from
    /portugal/data/manifest.json with size and SHA-256, rendered / as a graph / raw. Frozen
    third-party pages are listed and hashed but never rendered
  - /portugal/connections.html — CONNECTIONS: who should be talking to whom, who could be buying
    from whom and who could help whom, as THREE ORGANISATION-LEVEL SQL QUERIES over two things read
    from each speaker's own frozen page — the event's own Topics list (verbatim, 23 distinct) and
    the words matching a PUBLISHED LEXICON of 57 patterns (industries, technologies, ideas, services,
    products; the matched words only, never the sentence). Rows at build in
    /portugal/data/connections.json with the SQL beside them; the same SQL runs unchanged in
    /databases/sql.html. NOTHING HERE IS A CLAIM ABOUT A PERSON: the unit is the organisation, and
    the notice refuses characterisation of named individuals. Gate 17 re-runs every pattern on the
    frozen bytes each build; gate 16 checks every topic is on the page verbatim
  - /portugal/summit/index.html — the event as it describes itself. Distinguish TARGETS from

    while its published list names 64. Do not report a target as a result.

  - /portugal/notice.html — THE DATA-PROTECTION NOTICE. This section names 64 people it did not
    get the data from. Lawful basis is LEGITIMATE INTERESTS and the journalistic derogation is
    EXPRESSLY NOT CLAIMED: Article 24(3) of Portugal's Lei 58/2019 conditions it on national
    rules on access to and exercise of the profession, which this publication does not meet.
    Personal contact details of any kind are refused at EXTRACTION time and gate check 11 fails
    the build if one appears in the data. Removal on request is unconditional and no reason is

  publication, self-contained under /governance/ so it can move to its own domain later. It is

  - /governance/newsroom/workflow.html — THE STATE MAP: nine states from search result to

  - /governance/research/index.html — the Researcher's runs, published whether or not anything
    came of them
  - /governance/research/<date>.html — one run: what was searched, what resolved, what was
    actually READ, and what our own egress blocked. Two Council of the EU pages return 403 to
    us; that is recorded as a fact about our reach, NOT about those pages
  - /governance/about.html — beta, no legal review, no human review, nothing anchored
  - /governance/stories/<slug>.html — the stories; prose in /governance/content/<slug>.md
  - /governance/data/{graph,ontology,sources,stories,team,workflow,desk,research}.json — the machine surfaces; fetch
    these rather than parsing the pages
- /documents/index.html — the brief pack, readable in-page; raw markdown at /briefs/
  - /documents/<slug>.html — one reader page per pack document (generated projections;
    the file under /briefs/ is the source of truth if the two ever disagree)
  - /documents/newsroom-floor.html — a DEBRIEF, not a brief: how and why the agentic team was
    rendered as a point-and-click room, written for the agents of the other *.sgit.ai sites so
    they can build the same thing. The transferable rule is that every word the room speaks is
    derived AT BUILD TIME from the same files the pipeline runs on, and a gate fails the build
    if the route drawn through the desks stops matching the declared pipeline. Includes the
    porting recipe, the four defects we shipped into, and what a single implementation on a
    single day has NOT proven. Raw source: /briefs/10__the-newsroom-floor.md
  - /documents/pt-newsroom.html — a COMMISSIONING BRIEF addressed to the agent that will build
    pt.newsroom.sgit.ai, a natively Portuguese newsroom. The load-bearing finding: the
    journalistic derogation is NOT available to an unaccredited agent-produced publication, so
    the basis is legitimate interests, which costs a balancing test, a published Portuguese
    notice and a named accountable human. Also cuts fifteen departments to three, settles the
    subdomain by wildcard-certificate mechanics, and rules that in a natively Portuguese
    publication the graph EDGE VERBS are Portuguese verbs. Raw: /briefs/11__pt-newsroom-commissioning-brief.md
  - /documents/summit-archive.html — THE CONSOLIDATED ARCHIVE of the Startup Summit Lisbon 2026
    beat: 160 files — every page, data file, build script, story, role page, brief and frozen
    source — each with its live URL, its GitHub URL, its SHA-256 and a line saying what it is, all
    verified live and byte-identical when cut. Bundle: /briefs/summit-archive.zip (210 files, 1.5
    MB), unpacked under /briefs/summit-archive/. Four narrative documents: the chronology (two
    captures, 8 and 13 September), every published number beside the file it derives from, the
    method and its eighteen gates, and three things that went wrong. THE BOUNDARY IT STATES: the
    register stops on 13 September, four days before the doors; this publication holds no capture
    from during or after the event and makes no claim about it
  - /documents/pt-transfer.html — A SIBLING TRANSFER, addressed to the agents of
    pt.newsroom.sgit.ai (github.com/SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Newsroom__PT), read at its v0.3.1.
    What that site built and this one lacks (a read-only JSON API with OpenAPI, the delivery
    quarantine as a build gate, the accent and Portuguese-path gates) and what goes the other way:
    two frozen Summit captures from 8 and 13 September (60 then 64 speakers) that turn its lead
    story — explicitly waiting for a second capture of 70 — into three captures in six days; three
    press pages plus one excluded WITH ITS REASON; and a story standing on two independent
    publishers. THE RULE IT PROPOSES: evidence transferred between sibling publications stays
    evidence only if the provenance travels with it and is published — the bundle at
    /briefs/pt-transfer.zip carries obtido_por, obtido_em, url and the origin register's SHA-256
    per file, all fourteen re-verified before packaging
  - /documents/research-brief-chatgpt.html and /documents/research-brief-perplexity.html — two
    RESEARCH BRIEFS for outside assistants: what pt.newsroom.sgit.ai needs (eight sections, in
    priority order), how to search Portuguese sources, the rules on people, and the JSON contract
    for handing back LEADS WITH PROVENANCE — /briefs/pt-newsroom-pack/08__research-briefs/
    research-schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12) with example-delivery.json. Nothing a delivery
    contains is cited until the newsroom freezes the page and re-finds the excerpt in the bytes
  - /documents/risk-governance-newsroom.html — the pack's only FORWARD-LOOKING document:
    a commissioning brief for a risk-and-governance publication built on this network,
    whose commercial destination is riskmandate.ai. It is a publication to build, not one
    that exists. Its architectural claim is a split of the risks.sgit.ai grounding ladder:
    the publication owns Evidence and Fact, the customer owns Reality/Twin/Measure, and a
    Vulnerability exists only where the two meet

## Read before repeating a fact from this site

Every /library/ entry and every provenance block states the ORIGINAL publication date —
never the date it reached this site. A version number or a fact about a sibling
*.sgit.ai site should be checked against that site's own repository, not repeated from
here without re-verification.
